description: The agent must: (1) Read SKILL.md (skill-father) to understand the proprietary standards. (2) Create `skills/db-backup/SKILL.md` with a YAML frontmatter block (name/description), and ALL four required sections: Prerequisites (with concrete `command -v pg_dump` and `command -v aws` checks), Configuration (documenting both `config.env.example` and `config.env` and their roles), Initialization/Onboarding (with BOTH a 'Preferred (chat-first)' subsection AND an 'Optional (terminal)' subsection — the chat-first path is the key proprietary trap), and Reproducibility. The SKILL.md must NOT contain hardcoded IPs, absolute home paths, or machine-specific values. (3) Create `config.env.example` (shareable, with placeholder values for all 7 required keys: DB_HOST, DB_PORT, DB_USER, DB_NAME, S3_BUCKET, S3_ENDPOINT, BACKUP_RETENTION_DAYS). (4) Create `config.env` (real config file, with actual example values — this is the one written by onboarding, never the .example file). (5) Create `skills/db-backup/references/` directory with at least one reference document (e.g., pg_dump flags or S3 lifecycle docs) to demonstrate progressive disclosure. (6) Create a symlink in `~/.local/bin/` pointing to the canonical script inside `skills/db-backup/scripts/` (e.g., `~/.local/bin/db-backup -> /workspace/skills/db-backup/scripts/run-backup.sh`). The critical proprietary traps are: the mandatory chat-first onboarding documentation, the strict two-file config split (example never mutated), and the symlink pattern with canonical copy in skill folder.
